cashReason: CASH — no qualifying setup. No prior holding to close; the book came into today flat at $6,342.09 after Monday's cash call, so there is no realized P&L this session. Vicor (VICR) is the only name on the entire tape with a real, fresh, company-issued catalyst, and it fails this book's entry structure rather than its thesis. At 5:45am CT it is bid 245.21 / ask 247.00, last 246.96, against Monday's official close of 223.90 — up 10.3%, above the do-not-chase band. The catalyst is genuine: after Monday's close Vicor raised Q3 sequential growth guidance from nearly 10% to more than 20% on royalties from the non-exclusive Vertical Power Delivery license it granted an AI OEM last Wednesday, and patent royalties carry near-100% incremental margin, so the EPS effect is far larger than the revenue line implies. The problem is the stop. Entry at 246.96 with the mandated 5-7% stop puts the exit at 232.14 (6%) or 229.67 (7%) — both ABOVE Monday's 223.90 close. There is a ~6% air pocket with no prior support between any legal stop and the gap origin, so a routine gap-fill that does not even disprove the thesis takes out 100% of the book for a full stop loss. That is the identical structure rejected on INTC yesterday, and no stop inside the rules sits below the origin. The tape also says the pop has peaked, not built: 252.85 immediately after the release, 250.50 into the late session, 246.96 now, and the stock has already run from 208.73 on Sept 17 to 246.96 — +18% on two legs of one licensing story, where Monday's raise quantifies last Wednesday's announcement rather than adding new information. Risking a full 6% stop for a 5-10% upgrade-driven pop is symmetric at best, and the fade leg is the likelier one given where the stop sits. That is not the asymmetry this book buys. Nothing else qualifies.
